questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India CANNOT be amended with simple majority?
questions.solution: Article 21 (Protection of Life and Personal Liberty) is a fundamental right and requires a special majority of Parliament (as per Article 368) for any amendment. Contrast: Articles 2, 3 (creation of states), and 169 (abolition or creation of Legislative Councils) can be amended by a simple majority, as the Constitution specifically states these changes are not to be deemed amendments under Article 368.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deal with citizenship?
questions.solution: Articles 5 to 11 under Part II of the Constitution deal with citizenship. These provisions only identify persons who became citizens at the commencement of the Constitution (Jan 26, 1950). Note: It empowers Parliament (under Article 11) to enact laws to regulate the right of citizenship, which led to the Citizenship Act, 1955.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour?
questions.solution: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour (begar). It is a right against exploitation and is available against both the State and private individuals. Related: Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below 14 years in factories or hazardous conditions.

questions.question: Which Clause of Article 20 incorporates the doctrine of double jeopardy?
questions.solution: Article 20 (2) incorporates the doctrine of double jeopardy, which states that 'no person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once.' Scope: This protection applies only to proceedings before a court of law or a judicial tribunal.

questions.question: Article 20 of the Constitution of India is related to _____.
questions.option_2: protection in respect of conviction for offenses
questions.option_4: equality of opportunities in matters of public employment
questions.solution: Article 20 provides protection in respect of conviction for offences. It includes three distinct safeguards: (1) No ex-post-facto law, (2) No double jeopardy, and (3) No self-incrimination. Note: This is one of the two articles (along with Art 21) that cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution states that ‘It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.’?
questions.solution: Article 51A (e) is the fundamental duty to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood. It also mandates the renunciation of practices derogatory to the dignity of women. This duty aims to transcend religious, linguistic, and regional diversities to foster national unity.

questions.question: In which judgement did the Supreme Court extend the scope of Article 21 and observed that ‘the Right to education flows directly from the Right to life’?
questions.option_1: Kharak Singh v State of UP
questions.option_2: Malak Singh v State of Punjab
questions.option_3: Neerja Choudhari v State of M. P.
questions.option_4: Mohini Jain v State of Karnataka
questions.solution: In the Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka (1992) case (also known as the 'Capitation Fee Case'), the Supreme Court held that the Right to Education flows directly from the Right to Life (Article 21). Evolution: This was later refined in the Unni Krishnan case and eventually led to the 86th Amendment Act adding Article 21A.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles was amended by The Constitution Fiftieth Amendment Act, 1984?
questions.solution: The 50th Amendment Act, 1984 amended Article 33 to expand the power of Parliament to restrict or abrogate the fundamental rights of persons employed in intelligence organizations or telecommunication systems set up for the armed forces or intelligence agencies. Purpose: To ensure the proper discharge of their duties and maintenance of discipline.

questions.question: _________ Fundamental Duties were added in Part-IV of the Constitution under Article 51-A in the year 1976 through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment.
questions.solution: Ten Fundamental Duties were originally added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. They were incorporated based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. Update: The 11th duty was added later in 2002 by the 86th Amendment.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are INCORRECT vis-à-vis features of the Indian Constitution?

1) Though India has a federal system, the Constitution does not mention the word ‘federation’.

2)Article 5 of the Constitution says that the Parliament by law can create a new state.

3) On the subjects in the Union list, each State Legislature can enact laws for the State.

4)Both the Parliament and State Legislature can pass laws on subjects in concurrent list.
questions.solution: Statements 2 and 3 are INCORRECT. Article 3 (not 5) empowers Parliament to create new states. Also, subjects in the Union List are under the exclusive jurisdiction of the Parliament, not the State Legislatures. Correct Fact: Statement 1 is true—the word 'federation' is never used in the text of the Constitution.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution mentions that “the Parliament consists of the President and two Houses known as the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha)”?
questions.solution: Article 79 defines the Constitution of Parliament. It states that the Parliament for the Union shall consist of the President and two Houses: the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha). Note: Though the President is not a member of either House, they are an integral part of Parliament.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution mentions about establishing and maintaining institutions for religious and charitable purposes?
questions.solution: Article 26 provides every religious denomination the right to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes. This is part of the 'Freedom of Religion' (Articles 25-28). Distinction: Article 25 is for individual rights, while Article 26 covers the rights of religious denominations/groups.

questions.question: In a situation wherein A (female) and B (male) are working in same office, same designation, same nature of work but unequal payment, which of the following Articles of the Constitution will be applicable?
questions.solution: Article 39(d) (a Directive Principle) provides for equal pay for equal work for both men and women. While not a fundamental right itself, the Supreme Court has often read it alongside Article 14 to enforce wage parity in similar job roles.

questions.question: Which Articles of the Constitution deal with citizenship?
questions.solution: Articles 5 to 11 are the specific set of articles dealing with citizenship at the time of the Constitution's commencement. Article 5 deals with citizenship at the domicile, while Article 11 gives Parliament the power to regulate citizenship by law.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are INCORRECT vis-à-vis Fundamental Duties?

1) The 44th amendment Act introduced Fundamental duties in the Constitution.

2) Fundamental Duties were expanded by the 86th amendment act.
questions.option_1: 3) Article 51A entails respect its ideals and institutions, national flag and the national anthem. 4) Fundamental Duty obliges parents to provide opportunities for education to their child between 6-14 years of age.
questions.solution: Statement 1 is INCORRECT. Fundamental Duties were introduced by the 42nd Amendment Act (1976), not the 44th. True Facts: The 86th Amendment added the 11th duty, and Article 51A(a) requires respect for the National Flag and Anthem.

questions.question: Under the discretionary power of which Article of the Indian Constitution did the SC of India recognise sex work as a profession?
questions.solution: The Supreme Court used its discretionary powers under Article 142 to recognize sex work as a profession. Article 142 allows the court to pass any order necessary for doing 'complete justice' in any cause or matter pending before it. Context: This allows the court to fill legislative vacuums in the interest of justice.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are INCORRECT vis-à-vis Fundamental Duties?

1) They are obligatory in nature

2) Fundamental Rights and Fundamental duties are complementary to each other.

3) The introduction of Article 51A created strong base for a concrete national character and strong harmony.

4) Eleventh fundamental duty was added by 78th constitutional amendment act.
questions.solution: Statement 4 is INCORRECT. The eleventh fundamental duty was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, not the 78th. Core Concept: Fundamental Duties are civic obligations that complement the rights of citizens to create a balanced social contract.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles in the Constitution of India provides protection to President and Governors and Rajpramukhs?
questions.solution: Article 361 provides protection/immunity to the President and Governors. They are not answerable to any court for the exercise of their powers and duties, and no criminal proceedings can be instituted against them during their term of office.

questions.question: Which Article provides that all minorities have the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice?
questions.solution: Article 30 grants all minorities, whether based on religion or language, the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. It also prevents the State from discriminating against such institutions while providing financial aid.

questions.question:
A school teacher asks students to stand up every time national anthem is sung.

Which Article enshrines this fundamental duty?
questions.solution: Article 51A (a) enshrines the fundamental duty to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag, and the National Anthem.

questions.question: Which set of Articles in the Constitution of India are known as ‘Cultural and Educational Rights’?
questions.solution: Articles 29 and 30 are known as 'Cultural and Educational Rights'. Article 29 protects the interests of minorities by allowing them to conserve their language, script, or culture, while Article 30 allows them to run their own educational institutions.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles was amended in the Constitution (Fifth Amendment Act), 1955?
questions.solution: The 5th Amendment Act, 1955 amended Article 3. It empowered the President to specify a time limit for State Legislatures to express their views on proposed central legislation that affects the area, boundaries, or name of that state.

questions.question: _________ of the Constitution of India has provisions for legal enforcement of the fundamental rights.
questions.solution: Article 32 provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies, which is the mechanism for the legal enforcement of fundamental rights. It allows citizens to approach the Supreme Court directly. Significance: Without Article 32, fundamental rights would be mere 'pious declarations' without teeth.

questions.question: Lal Thanhawla holds the record for the longest-serving Chief Minister of ________, occupying the position for five terms.
questions.solution: Lal Thanhawla is a prominent political leader who served as the Chief Minister of Mizoram for five terms. He is a member of the Indian National Congress and played a major role in the development of the state following the 1986 Mizoram Peace Accord.
